Subject: Clarify scoping for pen test we commissioned with SecureLabs

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for coordinating. We engaged SecureLabs to run the penetration test next month and they asked for a clear in-scope boundary. Our security team is trying to confirm exactly which Redwood-managed components we can and cannot include. Specifically:

- Is Redwood's multi-tenant Hosted API (the public endpoints customers call) considered in-scope for a customer-commissioned test, or is that only covered by Redwood's internal/third-party assessments?
- For Dedicated (reserved capacity) instances that Acme has reserved, are those clusters fully in-scope?
- For our Private VPC deployment (peered VPC + customer-managed routers) and the on-prem install we plan next quarter, what parts are considered your responsibility vs ours for testing?

SecureLabs is asking for network ranges, a list of assets we can hand them, and whether they get a test account on the dedicated clusters or need to go through a staging tenant. They also requested sample redacted PT reports from prior audits to understand level of detail.

Appreciate any clarification we can share with them today — they need to finalize the Statement of Work (SoW).

Best,
Tom

Hi Tom — quick summary below and I’ve put Dev, Mina, and Laura on the thread to provide the technical inventory and legal notes. Short answers up front: Hosted (multi-tenant public API) is NOT in-scope for customer-commissioned pen tests; Dedicated, Private/VPC, and on-prem can be scoped as in-scope with specific caveats.

High-level scoping guidance (policy):
- Hosted API (our multi-tenant service): out-of-scope for customer-commissioned tests. Redwood performs our own 3rd-party assessments and internal pen tests — customers may request summary artifacts (redacted high-level report, SOC2) but we do not allow external testers to directly probe the shared hosted control plane or tenant proxies.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): in-scope when the customer has exclusive tenancy. That includes the dedicated GPU nodes, load balancers provisioned for the customer, and any dedicated management agents (subject to agreed constraints). We require a test window and an approved test plan.
- Private / VPC deployments: in-scope for the components that run under the customer's VPC. For peered-network setups we consider the customer-controlled VPC and customer-owned routing infrastructure in-scope; Redwood-managed peering endpoints and any cross-account control-plane interfaces are in-scope only if agreed up front.
- On-prem package: in-scope for all customer-installed components (installer, runtime agents). Redwood provides a list of management ports, administrative accounts, and recommended test accounts.

We can provide a redacted prior pen test report (example, with customer-identifying details removed) and our dedicated-inventory CSV. See attachments: redwood-scope-explainer-20270118.pdf and redwood-dedicated-inventory-20270118.csv.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev/Laura to provide an asset list and IP ranges for the Dedicated clusters (attached CSV).
2) Agree a test plan that restricts DOOM-of-service tests against customer production; if Acme wants destructive tests we need separate approval and backups.
3) Confirm whether SecureLabs needs test accounts or will authenticate through your staging tenant.
4) Legal to sign our tester access addendum (I’ll route).

Dev/Laura/Mina — can you add the inventory, management plane endpoints, and required tester constraints? I want to give SecureLabs a single doc for the SoW by EOD.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Security Programs, Redwood Inference

> Dev/Laura/Mina — can you add the inventory, management plane endpoints, and required tester constraints? I want to give SecureLabs a single doc for the SoW by EOD.

Hi all — inventory + technical clarifications below (kept concise for the SoW). I attached the CSV with Dedicated cluster rows and IP ranges.

What we consider in-scope for Acme's commissioned test (technical):
- Dedicated clusters:
  - Tenancy: Dedicated GPU nodes assigned to Acme (cluster IDs in attached CSV).
  - Reachability: External endpoints fronting the dedicated cluster (customer-facing load balancers) and SSH bastion jumpbox for admin access (jumpbox only with pre-arranged credentials).
  - Management plane: The customer-specific management agent (redwood-agent) running inside the dedicated tenancy — testing allowed against agent endpoints listed in CSV.
- Private/VPC:
  - In-scope: Customer VPC resources (instances, routing rules) and peered endpoints that live in Acme VPC.
  - Out-of-scope by default: Redwood control plane endpoints that exist outside the peered VPC unless Acme explicitly requests them and Redwood legal signs the addendum.
- On-prem installation:
  - In-scope: All installed runtime components, admin consoles, and local storage mounts.
  - We provide a checklist of required logs and backup points before the test.

Tester constraints / required controls:
- No probing of Redwood internal multi-tenant control plane or shared databases.
- All tests must use Acme-specific credentials or pre-provisioned test accounts. No wildcard scanning of 10.0.0.0/8 without prior written consent.
- Scheduled test window and emergency rollback contact list (we’ll provide ops pager and runbook for test-hours).

Assets & IP ranges (high level):
- Dedicated cluster IPs: 34.205.120.0/24, 52.16.45.0/24 (see attached CSV for exact cluster rows).
- Management agent endpoint (per-cluster): agent-<cluster-id>.mgmt.redwood.internal (we can provide FQDNs for the SoW).

I can provide one-line allowed test cases and a pre-approved list of disallowed destructive tests. If Acme/SecureLabs want to include the Redwood peering endpoints or control-plane APIs, we need to run that through our legal and Slack the security on-call to sign off (this is unusual but possible for enterprise customers under NDA).

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
